Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are Ouija boards really dangerous in a way that a demonic entity can be let in?
Old_Answer: Yes. The imagination is one of the most important, potent, creative faculties at mankind’s disposal. The use of speculation, when it comes to matters involving the future, whether it is in “sports” like gambling on the horses or the slot machine, or using a “magic” board to let you in on secrets makes the human mind search for the unknown and to some extent unknowable (except through God) IN the unknown… It’s like going to a ballot box and voting on Door Number 1 without knowing what is behind door number 1. This kind of non-thinking, yet pining for some sort of “significant” or meaningful result raises the fear or anxiety level in a person, which also makes one prone to grasp any straw that volunteers itself. If the good can come through this way (and it doesn’t, for the good is not imprecise nor wishy washy nor speculative per se), then so can the bad. Therefore, stay away from these things. It is your desire to have something for free (as opposed to seeking counsel from God with whom you are in a relationship) that allows the dark side to bind you. You are volunteering for the bondage. Why go slave when you can be a free man?
Answer_with_writing_sample: Thank you for this intriguing question! In my view, the concern around Ouija boards being dangerous hinges not just on the boards themselves, but rather on the mindset and intentions of those engaging with them. It's easy to get caught up in the allure of inviting a spirit to chat, and I think many people don't fully consider the implications of what they might be opening the door to—metaphorically speaking, of course. There’s a good chance some folks enter the experience casual and carefree, thinking it's akin to a poker game, while others approach it with fear or reverence, which can almost act as an invitation for negative energies or entities. The phenomenon behind Ouija boards often seems less about the board and more about the energies conjured by collective belief and expectation. It’s like throwing a party: if you have good vibes and intentions, you might just have a great time; but if someone shows up with a chip on their shoulder, you could end up with chaos. So, it's not just a board; it’s a reflection of the participants’ collective mindset—one that can work for or against them. Mindfulness and respect in any spiritual endeavor, even one that might seem like a bit of fun with friends, are paramount because you never know what you might invite in!
Answer_with_user_profile: The belief that Ouija boards can invite demonic entities is largely rooted in cultural myths, psychological factors, and anecdotal experiences. While some people claim to have had negative encounters after using a Ouija board, there is little scientific evidence to support the idea that these boards can truly summon spirits or entities. Most researchers suggest that the phenomena experienced—such as movement of the planchette—can be attributed to the ideomotor effect, where people involuntarily move the pointer due to subconscious thoughts. In many cases, those who report feeling a presence or having a frightening experience may be influenced by the ambient atmosphere, personal beliefs, or even suggestive influences from others. However, some people do take Ouija boards seriously, often viewing them as portals to the spiritual realm. For them, the board may represent an invitation to engage with the unknown, leading to a psychological openness to experiences that may be interpreted as spiritual or otherworldly. While it's essential to approach the use of Ouija boards with caution and a critical mindset, the notion that they are inherently dangerous or can invite demonic entities leans more toward superstition than fact. Setting intentions, maintaining a respectful attitude, and being aware of one's mental state can mitigate fears associated with Ouija boards. Ultimately, whether one considers them dangerous often reflects personal beliefs rather than any objective reality regarding their use.
Answer_with_full_information: The debate around Ouija boards and their potential risks has been ongoing for years. While many people view these boards as a mere harmless game, others are convinced of their dangers, particularly concerning the idea of inviting negative entities into one’s life. From a psychological standpoint, it's crucial to recognize that the experience with an Ouija board often hinges on the beliefs and expectations of the participants. For some, the board acts as a tool for curiosity and exploration, while others believe it might open a portal to malevolent spirits. There's a psychological phenomenon known as the ideomotor effect, where individuals unknowingly allow their subconscious movements to influence the planchette's movement. This can lead to the feeling of communicating with spirits, making it more about the user's state of mind than any actual supernatural force. However, for those who truly believe in the possibility of encountering demonic entities, the fear and anxiety surrounding the board can become a self-fulfilling prophecy. It's important to remember that fear can lead to heightened sensitivity to strange occurrences, making people attribute their experiences to supernatural causes. If you're genuinely interested in using an Ouija board, approach it with respect, a clear intent, and an understanding of your own beliefs. Ultimately, while it's easy to sensationalize the potential dangers of Ouija boards, they primarily reflect the personal beliefs and experiences of the individuals using them rather than an inherent threat. So if you're cautious and aware, they might just be an interesting conversation starter, rather than a gateway to danger

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the one thing you feel you need to have to be truly content with your life, and what all would you sacrifice to get it?
Old_Answer: Number one thing: Reparations to all I have done wrong to or harmed, financially or otherwise. Especially, to my son, now an adult, whom I wronged through mistreatment. What all would I sacrifice to get it? First, my limited mindset about how best to produce financially has to go. Heretofore, I have operated out of only one framework: Start at the bottom, work hard, and rely on others to advance you. I need a better strategy. Presently, my son (and roommate) brings in more income than I; he is putting more money out for our overhead. It is reasonable, therefore, to be experiencing pressure to do better, both from within, and from without. Old habits die hard. They must be replaced by new ones with more payoffs. The biggest temptation is to hurry up and end the pain of cognitive dissonance, to get back up on that horse again, to once again join the majority of America’s lower-wage earners in a job with no benefits, where you don’t even know your schedule or number of hours from week to week, let alone are enabled to participate in a health insurance network that is worth your heard earned dough. But at least I’d be “doing my best,” right? “Doing right,” by “carrying my fair share,” isn’t that right? WRONG. All I would be doing is all that I have ever done before and it has NEVER worked. It ISN’T realistic that such an approach would ever work; it is an approach that has only functioned to bind me, to keep me down. You sit there in those positions, doing your best, all the while stilling your anger and discontent and reality-based worry about your future, thinking, “I’m doing the right thing;” Consoling yourself, “What else can be done?” Repeating mantras like, “It isn’t all my fault, that’s just the way things are.” Or worst of all, “Don’t worry, it’ll all be over soon.” I cannot and will not do that crap ever again in my life, period. So…. NEW STORY!! I’m flying off, like a straight-edged tangent, bouncing off that circle of enclosure over options that will never open to a different reality, earnestly applying myself instead to simple things, in order to change what has been the status quo in my life for years. I am shutting down what has been my modus operandi and risking being exposed for a phony, an ignoramus, an under-achiever who’s actually just stupid, or dumb, or whatever I think I might “really” be. Simple things first: I am treating my son with more kindness; finding ways to negotiate and stand up for myself with less scream and more “you and me,” not just me; focusing on progress and insisting I make some; making sure there’s something in it for him. In so doing, I am protecting that part of me that conceives; the heart/spirit/brain-womb in me, that captures reality potential floating through the air, that cannot lite upon the dry hard pan ground of sheer drudgery. Instead, I am refusing to off that fertile body’s offspring before it gets a chance to grow. I am protecting it, and in so doing, I am protecting me. Interestingly enough, it seems that baby ideas, like little babies in the human womb, only survive in safety, with something to hang onto. It’s not enough that an idea is good. Or, perhaps in respect of one of America’s biggest over achievers, Jeff Bezos, I can agree that inspiration is 1%, 99% of success is in execution. The support of branches, of a sturdy vine, a labyrinth of options to shelter that baby from what would strike it down, is what comes next. Therefore, besides setting aside many personal patterns related to having a work life that’s DOA, another sacrifice I must make is to let go of control in the establishing of and maintenance of relational connection with others. For the ideas I wish to incubate are nearly all related on one level or another to community building; I like seeing other people pick up the power cords to their own abilities and plug them in. Most of my ideas are related to improving the chances of that happening for individuals by establishing frameworks for community interaction that highlight both needs and opportunities - where the exposures of both of these sides of the coin of life exponentially increases the number of ways in which individuals can exert their own opinions and utilize their usually under-utilized skills, talents and abilities for the common good. I believe we human beings were made to function together like this. So, I am letting myself out of the prison yard of compulsion and death, and moving into the wilds of personal interactions with mindfulness of mutual respect and keeping an open mind, because you never know what you have that someone else needs, or what they have that you might need, or, in the case at hand, that your idea might need. My desire is to meet my goal of furnishing my son and others with full reparations by using my abilities to perceive and conceive, to let people see how amazing God is and what good ideas He has by setting aside all my junk and let HIM birth good stuff out of me. Thank you for asking to answer this, Mr. Deer. I hope it is helpful to some one out there.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Thank you for this thought-provoking question! The one thing I feel I absolutely need to be truly content in my life is a deep sense of balance—between work and play, productivity and relaxation, my needs and the needs of others. I think to achieve such harmony, I would be ready to sacrifice a few things—like the relentless pursuit of money for the sake of stature or a constant need for social validation. I would willingly let go of any toxic friendships or commitments that drain my energy and distract me from my true priorities. It’s all about carving out time for self-care, nurturing my passions, and connecting meaningfully with loved ones, even if it means stepping back from the rat race for a bit. Balancing these aspects doesn’t always come easily, but I firmly believe that the trade-off is worthwhile; it’s a recipe for true contentment in a world that often underscores chaos and competition. So, here's to finding that balance and cherishing what truly matters!
Answer_with_user_profile: To feel truly content with my life, the one thing I believe I need is a profound sense of connection—connection to people, to nature, and to a purpose greater than myself. Living in Colorado Springs, I am surrounded by the breathtaking beauty of the mountains, which often inspires me to hike and explore, fostering a deeper appreciation for nature. However, meaningful relationships with family and friends anchor my emotional well-being. To cultivate these connections, I would willingly sacrifice the superficial aspects of modern life: a high-paying job that demands more hours than it rewards, social media distractions that pull me away from real interactions, and the constant chase for material possessions that clutter my space and mind. I would prioritize time spent with loved ones over career ambitions, understanding that the joy of shared experiences and laughter is irreplaceable. I would also invest time in giving back to my community, whether volunteering or supporting local initiatives, as this enriches my life’s purpose. Ultimately, the sacrifices I would make for connection—like simple living or reduced professional aspirations—are minor compared to the fulfillment that comes from deep, authentic relationships and a genuine sense of belonging. For me, true contentment lies not in solitary achievements but in the bonds we forge and nurture along the journey of life.
Answer_with_full_information: To be truly content with my life, I believe the one essential thing is meaningful connection—whether that’s with family, friends, or even the community around me. In this fast-paced world, it can be all too easy to become consumed by personal ambitions or material pursuits. However, I've learned through my experiences in Colorado Springs that genuine relationships provide not only support but also an invaluable sense of belonging. In moments of reflection, I would willingly sacrifice certain comforts, like a more glamorous lifestyle or the relentless pursuit of career advancement, to nurture and maintain these connections. Time spent basking in the beauty of a sunset shared with loved ones or engaging in heartfelt conversations over coffee far outweighs any fleeting success. While society often glorifies individual achievement, I’ve come to realize that life’s most profound joys stem from shared laughter, trust, and the simple act of being present for each other. So for me, it's non-negotiable; my life’s contentment hinges on those deep, authentic ties that remind me I am not alone on this journey. Sacrificing superficiality for depth? That's a trade I’d make any day.

Yet, a Christian man named John G. Lake, who in his later years had a ministry in Spokane, Washington, where he was hated by the medical establishment because every time he prayed for people, the hospitals would be emptied. Now, even if we credit the angry doctors with good intentions (“How can you deceive people like this? Answer_with_writing_sample: When I pray for someone else's good, it's like sending a heartfelt care package straight to their spirit, isn't it? There’s this fascinating sense of connection that weaves us together in an almost tangible way. It’s not just about the words; it’s about the intention behind them, and my goodness, intentions can carry a weight of their own! What a marvelous reminder that the act of giving can transform not just the receiver but also the giver!

Overall, praying for someone else is not only an act of kindness that can uplift others, but it can also nourish your own spirit, reinforcing the interconnectedness we share as human beings trying to navigate life’s challenges together.
Answer_with_full_information: When you pray for someone else's good, several meaningful things can unfold. In this way, praying for someone else's good is not just an act of kindness but a powerful affirmation of hope, not just for them, but for the world around us.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How does Benny Hinn get people to fall down and act like they do once they are on the ground?
Old_Answer: I thought it was phony. I had a then-older friend who had a mess of a house, a terrible childhood, widowhood from a man whom she might have been surely better off without as he used to beat her and their son, and she LOVED Benny Hinn. She was also a VERY powerful “prayer” warrior. Phenomenal at prophecy, though extremely humble and nearly non-existent ego. When I would stop by or call and hear Benny Hinn in the background, I said nothing, but I would just think, perhaps as you or MANY others do, “Well, if that comforts her, more power to her!” WOW, was I arrogant. I had NO idea this stuff was real. I mean NONE. Makes sense though, doesn’t it? For some of us who jump to conclusions that because our experience hasn’t been a certain way, a certain experience must be manufactured, false, or made up? I think so. Well, after my friend died, my son and I were invited to visit a Friday night meeting with a lady “prophet” who “walked in healing” and so on, (those quotes mean she has the spiritual gift(s) of healing and prophecy). People were going up and “getting slain by the spirit.” I thought, okay, what the heck… when my son asked if he should go up. I said sure, if you want. My son has some very special gifts anyway, and I had learned to trust his judgment on certain things, but I sure as heck didn’t need it. He went up, the lady put her hand on his chest, without any force really, then looked up at him when he didn’t “go down.” She stepped back and thought, or prayed, or both, and then put her hand on him again, with a little more force, and WHOMP, he went down and stayed down. Now, skeptics may feel, or conclude, this is hocus pocus, she pushed him down. Nah, my kid was 6′2″ and 170 pounds then and I can guarantee he wasn’t “pushed” down… But, you say, auto-suggestion… Nah, my son IS gullible in some ways… but NOT in this manner. He takes spiritual stuff seriously. He knows it’s not a game and he doesn’t take anyone else’s word, including his mother’s, for anything. Stubborn “young” fool that he is. Anyway, truly, he sorts it all out himself. Well, he went down and stayed down for a bit; when he came back to the chair next to me, he just felt to me to be a bit more relaxed. Okay, REALLY relaxed. But he didn’t say much to me about it until much much later, a couple YEARS later. We went to visit Charis Bible College here in Colorado Springs, Colorado, one Sunday for a special healing service where they had arranged to bring in a world renown “healer.” He had called on the Wednesday prior to let them know he couldn’t make it…. he was worn out and needed rest, and so he cancelled What were Pastor Lawson Purdue and Andrew Wommack to do? Well, they decided to go ahead and have the event, and they put themselves wholly into the event. My son and I were sitting in the back. There was a long time period after a lesson of sorts, of people of all ages sizes and shapes ministering to those who asked for healing all around the large auditorium off of Elkton (this is before their move up to Woodland Park). A minister of Lawson’s came up to me when I was interceding while others were praying for a woman wheelchair-bound with multiple sclerosis. “Ma’am, Do you need healing?” “Oh, no, I’m fine, I’M PRAYING FOR OTHERS,” I proudly announced, because you see, NO ONE’S GONNA fool around with MY BODY, MY HEALING, MY SPIRITUAL LIFE…. I’m no fool!!!! Oh, but what a fool I was, my intellect pierced through with pride. Fortunately for me, the band of do-gooders around this one woman in the wheelchair dissolved, and all of a sudden, I find myself faced with this Texan in a 10-gallon hat, saying, loudly, “MA’AM, may I pray for your?” And barely before I could get a syllable out, this guy has his hand on my neck, and I start feeling this INCREDIBLE feeling, this warmth, like I have never felt before in my life, or since. AND THEN this thing started happening… It was like a humongous, hot flapping butterfly was on top of my head, flapping his wings up and down, up and down, but I wasn’t letting go. I looked around, I weigh a good deal, and I thought, I am not going down with catchers around me… there seemed to be none; the phenomenon continued, all of a sudden, my son was behind me with another man, THEN I remembered what my son had finally told me one day about his experience with that lady, “I just knew, Mom, that if I let go it would feel really, really, good.” I let go. BAM… I went down into those men’s arms and laid on that floor for a bit. I had never had anything like this happen to me, though I was filled with the Holy Ghost when I had a priest in the Episcopal Church lay his apostolic bishopy hand on my head for confirmation in sixth grade… (I began to speak in tongues afterwards but did not know what that was). But, the most amazing thing about this experience, is that it didn’t end. For TWO WEEKS solid, I was in another world. It was like, and believe, me, I had never ever ever put these silly sounding words together in the same sentence before, and no, no one told me this is what you say, or what not, but it was like a few drops of “golden anointing oil,” had been spread throughout my whole being. It was one of the loveliest experiences I have ever had in my life. So, that’s MY experience. But it wasn’t about Benny Hinn. This one is: Todd White was meeting a drug dealer. Addicted to porn by age 10, drugs by 12, this then teen-ager, had conceived the brilliant plan (a way to get yourself shot, actually) to cheat a drug dealer by pretending he was an undercover cop and demanding on the goods…. When the shots started to ring out from the dealer’s 9mm, White was standing next to his car and only about 10 to 12 feet I think it was from the gun. The bullets did not hit him; It was as though they went THROUGH HIM into other objects around him. He got in his car and sped off in total shock and freaked out then heard a voice, “I took those bullets for you, Todd.” Great, Todd thought, now I’m f***ed with the dealer, gonna get killed, AND I’m losing my mind. But there is was again. And then he told Todd he was Jesus. Which freaked him out ever more. So, without going into more detail, Todd was saved that night, and began growing in the Lord right away, but was not getting the results he wanted. He wanted his laying of hands on people to work, just the way the bible says. He wanted to see the blind see and the deaf hear and lame walk. So, he decided to try some Christian conferences. At one, he decided to sit up front. All of a sudden, the speaker pointed at him and told him to come up front. Todd was surprised, but went up. The man looked at Todd, who was several feet from him, with two very large men behind him to “catch” him or help if anything went down. All of a sudden, the man said something, made a move with his arm toward Todd, and TODD AND THE TWO CATCHERS went up in the air four feet and BACK six feet as they heard what sounded like crackling in the air… something like thunder. Todd was stunned, the catchers were caught off guard. And as Todd came around, and sat up and then stood up, he stood in front of the man once more, and said, “AGAIN.” BOOM, up four feet (with the other two BIG guys, again) and back six. Todd was discombobulated. Could not speak. Was receiving power from on high and did not know his name hardly. The two ushers gathered their wits, readied themselves to carry Todd off the stage, then the man of God said to the Man of God, “I NEED MORE OF JESUS;” and ONE MORE TIME. Todd, he says in more than one testimony, was reduced to tears. They literally had to carry him OFF stage, and set him on the floor, where he remained in tears, sobs and so forth for the rest of the event. Now, that man, Todd, he’s got some courage. And the man standing in for God to wipe him out and see that he would be imbued with God’s power? Benny Hinn.

Question: Since I moved back to my parents about 4 months ago, my father keeps getting really angry and talk pretty ugly to me, and most of the times he's around I feel like he really doesn't want me to be here. What's wrong with us…?
Old_Answer: Sorry to hear you are facing this kind of stress in the midst of an already weird and uncomfortable time. When my child was very young, say between four and six, we visited a store on the westside - a discount, re-sell place. They have the old circular clothing racks there, perfect for a child to hide under….! All of a sudden, though I kept really good watch over my son, he was gone! Inside, of course, I panicked! Then I saw some clothing moving under a rack a good 15 feet away from me, and was so relieved to find him under there. I remember doing the same thing myself when my mom would drag me along to stores. BORING! And that’s what I thought this kind of behavior is about… just being bored and looking to play. Years later, however, my son told me one reason why kids might do that behavior. The young of other mammals, and our little children as well, “know” when mom, their chief protector most of the time, is TIRED. Running off to a safe, sheltered, dark place and hiding can be a defense mechanism that is based in instincts! What an insight! Makes total sense to me now! What does this have to do with your Dad? I’m thinking, instinctively, he is pushing you away and being hostile due to CO-VID 19 and its very real threats against your life and his. It is entirely unnatural to keep social distances up, especially with people we know… Doing so causes tension, and keeping on our toes about this practice makes many people (might I say ALL?) uptight. I think you might want to consider that your dad is worried, and at moments he might not even admit to himself, he is worried about somehow hurting YOU by being sick himself and not knowing it. Words won’t comfort him - he’s your dad, and if he loves you, he is still going to NOT want you to get sick or worse. Wear your mask, even at home… research shows there is a big spread amongst families whose members eat together and do things together, live watch tv, if they do it without masks. It seems weird to do it, but my family is doing it. Masks cannot control every little risk about this pandemic, but it slows transmission rates, even at home, among family members, as does the hand washing for more than 20 seconds… and keeping up with other hygiene, and laundry cycling on hot water and hot air for drying, and disinfecting high-touch surfaces like door knobs, faucet and drawer pulls and handles, light switches, electronic devices, and so on and so forth. See what you can do to contribute, and find sources of real support where you can let your hair down and get things off your chest… don’t try to resolve a bunch of family stuff right now. We’re all on docks that are shifting in the water and some of our docks’ posts are coming loose from their mooring. Give things time… I think Fall 2021 we will all be much better off and wiser. Now, however, is NOT the time to let up. Keep up all your efforts. In your heart of hearts, try to just take time to remind yourself of all that you value about your dad and other family members, and how much you have to look forward to, to live for, and to do in life, so that you can keep your motivation HIGH (and your example SUPERIOR) til this thing is over.
